t: Section 4(g) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 633(g)) is amended to read as follows:“(g) Business Opportunity Specialists.—“(1) Duties.—The exclusive duties of a Business Opportunity Specialist employed by the Administrator and reporting to the senior official appointed by the Administrator with responsibilities under sections 8, 15, 31, and 36 (or the designee of such official) shall be to implement sections 7, 8, and 45 and to complete other duties related to contracting programs under this Act. Such duties shall include—“(A) with respect to small business concerns eligible to receive contracts and subcontracts pursuant to section 8(a)—“(i) providing guidance, counseling, and referrals for assistance with technical, management, financial, or other matters that will improve the competitive viability of such concerns;“(ii) identifying causes of success or failure of such concerns;“(iii) providing comprehensive assessments of such concerns, including identifying the strengths and weaknesses of such concerns;“(iv) monitoring and documenting compliance with the requirements of sections 7 and 8 and any regulations implementing those sections;“(v) explaining the requirements of sections 7, 8, 15, 31, 36, and 45; and“(vi) advising on compliance with contracting regulations (including the Federal Acquisition Regulation) after award of such a contract or subcontract;“(B) reviewing and monitoring compliance with mentor-protege agreements under section 45;“(C) representing the interests of the Administrator and small business concerns in the award, modification, and administration of contracts and subcontracts awarded pursuant to section 8(a); and“(D) reporting fraud or abuse under section 7, 8, 15, 31, 36, or 45 or any regulations implementing such sections.“(2) Certification requirements.—“(A) In general.—Consistent with the requirements of subparagraph (B), a Business Opportunity Specialist described under section 7(j)(10)(D) shall have a Level I Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting (or any successor certification) or the equivalent Department of Defense certification.“(B) Delay of certification requirement.—The certification described in subparagraph (A) is not required—“(i) for any person serving as a Business Opportunity Specialist on the date of the enactment of this subsection, until the date that is one calendar year after the date such person was appointed as a Business Opportunity Specialist; or“(ii) for any person serving as a Business Opportunity Specialist on or before January 3, 2013, until January 3, 2020.“(3) Job posting requirements.—The duties and certification requirements described in this subsection shall be included in any initial job posting for the position of a Business Opportunity Specialist.”.

fable.w: The section sets out the duties, certification requirements, and job-posting requirements for Business Opportunity Specialists, who are federal employees of the Small Business Administration. The tempting reading is that counseling small businesses or "representing the interests of... small business concerns" is outside participation, but these are services and functions performed by a federal employee, not a process through which outside parties are consulted on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: The exclusive duties of a Business Opportunity Specialist employed by the Administrator

qwen_block.w: This section defines the duties and certification requirements for a federal employee (a Business Opportunity Specialist). The text explicitly states these specialists are 'employed by the Administrator' and report to other federal officials. There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or non-federal experts) in the decision-making process. The interaction described is internal to the federal government.
qwen_block.s: The exclusive duties of a Business Opportunity Specialist employed by the Administrator and reporting to the senior official appointed by the Administrator... shall be to implement sections 7, 8, and 45 and to complete other duties related to contracting programs under this Act.

opus.w: The section defines the job duties, certification requirements, and job posting rules for Business Opportunity Specialists, who are federal SBA employees. Their counseling of small businesses and representation of their interests are federal employees doing their jobs, not outsiders being consulted before a federal decision. The reference to 'regulations implementing those sections' only points to existing rules and creates no new rulemaking authority, so there is no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: The exclusive duties of a Business Opportunity Specialist employed by the Administrator and reporting to the senior official appointed by the Administrator

1. **Tempting-but-wrong readings:**
   - Business Opportunity Specialists work with small businesses: they counsel them and represent their interests in awarding contracts. That looks like a channel between the government and outsiders. But the specialists are SBA employees doing their jobs, and the small businesses are recipients of help and contract programs, not people being consulted before a federal decision.
   - The phrase "any regulations implementing those sections" might look like rulemaking. It only refers to regulations that already exist. It does not grant or require any new rulemaking.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the duties of federal employees (Business Opportunity Specialists) within the Small Business Administration. It describes internal agency operations, such as monitoring compliance and providing guidance to applicants, rather than a process where outside parties consult with the government before a decision is made. The specialists are federal employees, and their interactions with small businesses are part of the application and contract administration process, which is excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The exclusive duties of a Business Opportunity Specialist employed by the Administrator and reporting to the senior official appointed by the Administrator... shall be to implement sections 7, 8, and 45 and to complete other duties related to contracting programs under this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Business Opportunity Specialists" represent the interests of small business concerns (outside parties) and thus facilitate participation. However, the text explicitly states these specialists are "employed by the Administrator" (a federal official) and their duties are internal to the agency's contracting process (monitoring compliance, providing guidance to applicants). This is internal agency staffing and procedure, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with or influence federal decision-making. The interaction described is the agency providing services or enforcing rules on applicants, which falls under the "applications for benefits" or internal agency operation traps, not participation.
